_comment: THE FIXTURE WORLD. Every byte and every mtime is DECLARED here, because the
contract this suite records depends on both: the reader orders its index
newest-first by entry mtime, and `/api/v1/snapshot` preserves those mtimes
with sub-second precision on purpose. A store checked into git would lose
them (git stores no mtime), so the store is BUILT from this file on every
run and the goldens are reproducible because the world is.
Every name here is synthetic and every timestamp is in the year 2000 -- see

in the fraction. That is the one input shape a normalised tar destroys, and

alpha-notes._why: Populated, and the ONE scope carrying a .git/HEAD -- so X-Store-Revision answers something other than `unknown` and the refused-vs-absent pair has a header that could discriminate.

beta-notes._why: Populated, and the only scope `narrow-reader` may see.

hollow-set._why: An existing directory holding no entry file at all -- the `scope-empty` state, which must not render like an unreadable one.

rubble-heap._why: Every file in it is malformed -- the `scope-unreadable` state.

tagged-set._why: The ONE scope whose entries carry `tags:`. It exists so a `?tag=` row can find a MATCH over the wire rather than only the non-finding: a corpus that only ever sent a tag nothing carries would pass against a filter wired to nothing. One entry carries TWO tags and a `refs:` (so the two filters can be composed over the wire), one carries ONE of those tags, and one carries none -- so the filter has something to keep and something to remove on EITHER tag, and the two tags name different sets, which is what stops a row passing with the operand ignored. A NEW SCOPE rather than tags added to an existing entry, so the only pre-existing goldens that move are the ones that ENUMERATE scopes.

linked-set._why: The ONE scope whose entries carry `refs:`. It exists so a `?ref-to=` row can find a MATCH over the wire rather than only the non-finding: a corpus that only ever sent a ref nothing carries would pass against a filter wired to nothing. One entry carries the ref under the NEW key, one under the ACCEPTED OLDER `tasks:` spelling, and one carries none -- so the filter has something to keep, something to keep through the alias path, and something to remove.

principals.name: wide-reader
principals._why: Sees every scope. The authorized principal for most cases, and the only one that can write.

principals.name: narrow-reader
principals._why: alpha-notes EXISTS and this principal may not see it. That is the refused half of the refused-vs-absent pair.

principals.name: legacy
principals._why: A bare row: unrestricted scope, no identity, and refused on every write route.

_why: THE ARC REGISTRY'S JOURNAL, SEEDED, one JSON object per element, written one per line. It is
Go-only (the oracle serves no arc route and is never told about it), and `suite.py build-store`
writes it OUTSIDE the store tree, because `cairn-server` refuses to start with a journal inside
it. An EARLIER registration of gadget-rollout (no status: unknown) is superseded by a later one
(open), so the latest-wins fold is on the wire. gadget-rollout is homed in alpha-notes and
DECLARES beta-notes, so narrow-reader's arcs/beta-notes must NOT list it -- the home-scope
visibility rule (Q1) on the wire -- while widget-fix, homed in beta-notes with no status, is the
one arc narrow-reader can see. Every name, session id and time is synthetic, year 2000.
